FAQ

Questions.

What is SkyWatch MCP?

SkyWatch MCP connects your AI assistant to SkyWatch, so you can search, price and order satellite imagery in plain language. It uses the Model Context Protocol, the open standard assistants use to work with outside tools. There is no new app to learn.

Which assistants does it work with?

ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini and Perplexity. You add SkyWatch once in each assistant you use, then sign in with the same SkyWatch account.

How does ordering work?

Ask for what you need, for example the latest cloud-free image of a site under a price cap. The assistant searches the archive, shows you the best match with its capture date, cloud cover, resolution and price, and waits. Nothing is ordered until you confirm. Once you do, the order is placed and appears in your SkyWatch account.

Will anything be ordered without my confirmation?

No. Every order shows its price first and needs your confirmation in the conversation before it is placed.

Do our budgets and approvals still apply?

Yes. Your SkyWatch account carries the same roles, budgets and approval rules as the SkyWatch app and API. Spend from the assistant is tracked against the same budget, and orders that need approval follow your team’s existing process.

Do I need an API key?

No. You sign in with your SkyWatch account. If you don’t have one yet, you can create one when you get started.

What imagery can I order?

Archive imagery and new satellite tasking from optical, SAR and elevation sensors, from very high to low resolution. You can search by place name, coordinates, a bounding box or GeoJSON.

How is pricing calculated?

Prices are based on area, in dollars per square kilometre, and depend on the sensor and resolution. The assistant shows the full price before you confirm, and can compare offers side by side.

Can results go straight into ArcGIS Online?

Yes. Results can be published to ArcGIS Online as a map layer, so your team can use them right away.
